stories.headline: Israel votes today in an election that could end Netanyahu's run
body: Israelis vote today for all 120 seats in the Knesset, the first election since the 7 October 2023 attacks and the Gaza war.
Netanyahu's Likud-led bloc with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties faces a four-party opposition alliance led by ex-army chief Gadi Eisenkot.
Polls show a close race, and no party has ever won 61 seats alone, so smaller parties, including Palestinian-led ones, could decide who governs.
stories.joke: Polls say it's a dead heat. Coalition talks say: see you in three months.
stories.vc: A change in government could reshape Israel's defence-tech and cyber spending, which feeds one of the world's busiest startup scenes.

stories.headline: Serbia's student movement beats Vučić's party in a historic upset
body: The Student List, put forward by Serbia's long-running youth protest movement, won more than half the votes in Sunday's parliamentary election.
President Aleksandar Vučić conceded, and his Serbian Progressive Party came a distant second after 14 years in charge.
The students are now preparing coalition talks, with a presidential election due in December.
stories.joke: Students skipped class for two years and still aced the final exam.
stories.vc: A cleaner, more predictable Serbia could speed EU talks and open the door to more Western investment in the Balkans.

stories.headline: Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish chiefs fly to Tehran to calm US–Iran tensions
body: Top officials from the three countries behind the Mecca defence pact met Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran on Monday.
The group includes Saudi defence minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani army chief Asim Munir and Turkish spy chief Ibrahim Kalin.
The visit comes as the US threatens new strikes on Iran and fighting with Yemen's Houthis worries Riyadh.
stories.joke: Three neighbours walk into Tehran. The punchline depends on Washington.
stories.vc: Any easing around the Strait of Hormuz would cool oil and fertiliser prices, a relief for India's import bill.

stories.headline: 21 news publishers take India's data protection law to the Supreme Court
body: A group of 21 news publishers has challenged the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act in the Supreme Court.
They say its consent and erasure rules could force journalists to ask investigation subjects for permission and delete true stories.
The case is due to be heard today. Most of the law's provisions take effect in May 2027.
stories.joke: Dear corrupt official, may we please have your consent to expose you?
stories.vc: Startups handling personal data are watching closely: how the court reads the consent rules will shape compliance costs for everyone.

image.title: File:Supreme Court of India, inside buildings 02.jpg

stories.headline: Paytm's quarterly profit jumps more than 10x to ₹225 crore
body: Paytm made a net profit of ₹225 crore in the July–September quarter, up from ₹21 crore a year earlier.
Operating revenue rose 28% to ₹2,648 crore, and profit edged up from ₹220 crore in the previous quarter.
Total expenses rose 23% to ₹2,531 crore, slower than revenue.
stories.joke: Remember when Paytm's only profitable product was cashback? Times change.
stories.vc: Steady profits make Paytm a test case for whether India's listed new-age tech firms can grow and earn at the same time.

image.title: File:Vijay Shekhar Sharma, Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Paytm.jpg

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty snap a four-day losing streak
body: The Sensex rose 482.92 points to 73,606.75 on Monday, and the Nifty gained 153.20 to 22,753.20.
Metal and oil and gas stocks led the gains, while banking and insurance stocks were sold.
Midcap and smallcap indices both rose about 1%.
stories.joke: Four red days, one green day. Investors are calling it a trend.
stories.vc: Mid and small caps outrunning the index hints that risk appetite is back, good news for upcoming startup IPOs.

stories.headline: Anthropic officially files to go public under the ticker ANT
body: Anthropic filed for its IPO on Monday, showing $16.3 billion in revenue for the first half of 2026, up from $1.2 billion a year earlier.
Its operating loss shrank to $693 million, though its net loss hit $80.7 billion, mostly from noncash accounting for convertible debt.
About 250 customers spend $10 million or more a year, and over half of $100k+ customers use both the API and apps like Claude Code.
stories.joke: An $80.7 billion loss that's mostly paperwork. Accountants have never felt so seen.
stories.vc: Revenue up roughly 13x in a year sets the bar for every AI IPO that follows, and gives private AI rounds a public price to point at.

stories.headline: SpaceX lines up $40 billion from Apollo to lease AI chips
body: SpaceX has a binding commitment for about $40 billion to fund AI chips and data centre equipment, calling it the largest committed GPU financing.
An Apollo-managed entity will buy the hardware and lease it to SpaceX for about five years per batch.
The deal should close by year-end, with leases starting in the first half of 2027.
stories.joke: Rockets were too cheap a hobby, so SpaceX picked up GPUs.
stories.vc: Leasing instead of buying is becoming the standard way to fund AI compute, and private credit firms like Apollo are the new landlords.

stories.headline: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees
body: Microsoft confirmed it is offering buyouts to around 60,000 staff as it cuts costs for the AI era.
Employees at vice-president level and below on select teams in the US, Canada, India and the UK are eligible.
Xbox, Windows, Copilot and Finance are reported to be included, while data centre, sales and marketing staff are excluded.
stories.joke: Copilot, write me a farewell email. Make it sound voluntary.
stories.vc: Big Tech trimming headcount to fund AI spending frees up experienced engineers, a hiring opening for startups, including in India.

stories.headline: Bedrock Robotics raises $600M for self-driving excavators
body: Two-year-old Bedrock Robotics raised a $600 million Series C at a $4.1 billion valuation, co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital.
Its kit retrofits existing excavators to drive themselves, and they now work on paid construction sites in Nevada and Texas.
The company has raised nearly $1 billion since its 2024 founding.
stories.joke: Finally, a robot that wants the job nobody else wanted.
stories.vc: Retrofit kits sell into a huge installed base without building new machines, which is why investors pay up for physical AI that ships.

stories.headline: Instagram tests 90-minute videos to take on YouTube
body: Instagram is testing a new upload type called Features that lets creators post videos up to 90 minutes long.
It is a sharp turn after years of pushing short, vertical Reels.
Creators mostly earn little directly from Instagram today, while YouTube pays them a share of ad revenue.
stories.joke: Reels taught us 30 seconds was too long. Now here's an hour and a half.
stories.vc: Long video means more ad inventory, so how Meta shares that money will decide whether creators actually move over.
